pr_title: drivers: wifi: esp32: connect to highest signal AP
pr_body:
The station-mode channel scan method is currently set to WIFI_FAST_SCAN which ignores the signal strength and connects to the first channel found which may result in poor WiFi bandwidth.

Change the scan mode to scan all channels and connect to the channel with the highest RSSI.

Fixes #84488
pr_comments: Since `WIFI_FAST_SCAN` is also an option for `wifi_config.sta.scan_method`, would you mind providing a Kconfig parameter regarding to the preferred scan method  having `WIFI_ALL_CHANNEL_SCAN` as the default one?

issue_context.title: ESP32 WiFi Channel Selection
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
Using the default channel of `WIFI_CHANNEL_ANY`, I am seeing the station-mode connection being established on the 1st channel which happens to have the worst RSSI on this network.  Looking into the code, `esp_wifi_drv.c` correctly converts `WIFI_CHANNEL_ANY` to a value of 0 in `esp_wifi_set_config()`, so it seems that the first channel found is being used instead of the strongest.

**To Reproduce**
Use the wifi example app `samples/net/wifi/shell/` and issue the following commands which I did on an ESP32-S3 system:

```
uart> wifi scan
Scan requested

Num  | SSID                             (len) | Chan (Band)   | RSSI | Security        | BSSID             | MFP     
1    | IoT                              3     | 11   (2.4GHz) | -47  | WPA2-PSK        | xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx | Disable 
2    | IoT                              3     | 11   (2.4GHz) | -60  | WPA2-PSK        | xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx | Disable 
3    | IoT                              3     | 1    (2.4GHz) | -79  | WPA2-PSK        | xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx | Disable

uart> wifi status
Status: successful
==================
State: COMPLETED
Interface Mode: STATION
Link Mode: WIFI 4 (802.11n/HT)
SSID: IoT
BSSID: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
Band: 2.4GHz
Channel: 1
Security: WPA2-PSK
MFP: Disable
RSSI: -82
Beacon Interval: 3
DTIM: 0
TWT: Not supported
Current PHY rate : 0
```

**Expected behavior**
When `WIFI_CHANNEL_ANY` is specified the highest signal strength channel should be selected.

**Impact**
Poor performance and network drops in areas with multiple APs.  In my case, the AP on channel 1 was located 20m away and the AP on channel 11 was located 2m away and the ESP32-S3 always connected to channel 1 resulting in poor performance.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
Zephyr 4.0 and main at commit hash 4ed85eec2b0f0f9a1e0a51b977050b86906d7ae8.
comments: The drivers/wifi/esp32/src/esp_wifi_drv.c was not setting the `scan_method` to `WIFI_ALL_CHANNEL_SCAN`.  See PR #84490 for the fix.

review_comments: Enabling `WIFI_ALL_CHANNEL_SCAN` will guarantee scanning all as it says, however, it won't sort by signal strength. Adding `.sort_method` method to `WIFI_CONNECT_AP_BY_SIGNAL` would make sure that the selected AP is indeed the one with higher RSSI. This suggestion is not blocking the PR though. LGTM
Yes, I had that in an early version of this patch, but `WIFI_CONNECT_AP_BY_SIGNAL` has a value of 0, so it is enabled by default.  Should I add it for completeness?
If you can, please do. At least it makes it clear about its usage.
